questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I mostly looked at smaller cities, since they, compared to bigger ones, seem to bring people, and especially students, more together. Smaller cities are also easier and quicker to feel connected to and find your way around.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was the best four months - the only reason I don't give it 10, is because it was difficult to find proper information about the university prior to the exchange, which caused a bit of stress. But like everyone highlights: everything worked out in the end, so really I shouldn't have stressed.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not the easiest. Since the University of Copenhagen and University of Bologna have different timelines for the exchange, it was a very frustrating process. The uni of CPH wanted my Online Learning Agreement a long time before I was able to see the available courses at Bologna. But thankfully it worked out in the end.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Bolognas University was on holiday when I arrived... So there was very little assistance in the beginning. But again,the most frustrating thing was the difference between the University of Copenhagen and of Bologna.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Don't stress too much. It will all work out, and 100% be worth it.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had the number of a guy who has apartments for exchange students - so it was very easy for me. His name is Leif.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's best to live inside the city walls, from there everything is a walking distance away

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the apartments were better than others. You can ask Laif to get the number of the people staying in the apartment before you, so you can ask them questions.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, after accepting my place from the University of Copenhagen, I think they automatically applied for Bologna's Uni for me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can look at Unibo's webpage.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Overall quite sucessful, but it took some time to understand which courses where available at what semester, and which courses were only available for Masters students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at Unibo's webpage for exchange students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked the courses, some were better than others.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The MA classes were in general the same level as BA classes at University of CPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very interactive, focused a lot on discussions - not very formal.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Urban studies and climate change - Criminology of the borders - Humanitarian Communication - Introduction to Italian culture

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Criminology of the Borders was one of my favourite courses ever! I loved the professor and the subjects. Even though it was a MA course, I just showed up to the first lesson and asked the professor, if it was okay for me to take it. She said it was up to me - if I thought I would be able to understand, I was very welcome.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were about the same as in DK - but eating out and drinking was much cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't attend any

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None that I knew of

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I dont know

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take the train or Flix bus around Italy. There are so many beautiful cities to see. Look for when there are food/wine festivals in cities near Bologna.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Show up to the Erasmus events, especially in the beginning. Ask people in you class to grab a coffee or aperitif after class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Only the system in Bolognas university - the professors are very chill, often show up late, are bad at giving clear instructions for the exam, but often that also just means that its easier to pass the class.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and wine culture, the friendliness, the architecture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy, relax and drink wine

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont stress, it will work out in the end

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the people I met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes it was a bit challenging with my roomies, since we had many differences in how we lived, cooked and cleaned. But I grew from those experiences, remembering, that there are many different ways to do things, and my ways are not always the right one.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go go go, you won't regret it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
